findings.description: CON-SUP-112 specifies a timestamp in milliseconds since start but does not identify the start reference, so the timestamp in SYS-SUP-032 is ambiguous.
findings.requested_change: Define the timestamp reference and update the requirement after the product owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the report entity, but none identifies the watchdog reset represented by code 8.
findings.requested_change: Define the report entity for watchdog reset code 8 after the product owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 calls execution longer than the limit an overrun while requiring detection at expiry. SYS-SUP-004 leaves the treatment of completion exactly at the limit unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and state a consistent detection rule.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-014 requires an application-image integrity check, but CON-SUP-107 does not define its method or reference data, so a test cannot determine the expected outcome for a given image.
findings.requested_change: Define the image integrity method and reference data after the product owner decides them.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 specifies the CRC polynomial but not the other CRC parameters or the covered byte range, so SYS-SUP-016 does not determine a unique expected CRC.
findings.requested_change: Supply a complete CRC definition and covered data range.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 places fault-report transmission after safe-state entry and before reset; SYS-SUP-026 specifies only the latter ordering. SYS-SUP-032 also imposes a 10 ms reporting deadline while safe-state entry may take up to 50 ms.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the ordering and deadlines with the product owner and specify consistent obligations for report transmission.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-031 treats each watchdog reset as a detected fault, invoking the general fault reaction and reset request. CON-SUP-111 and CON-SUP-112 do not establish whether that reaction is intended for code 8.
findings.requested_change: Decide and specify the reporting and recovery behavior after a watchdog reset.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 and SYS-SUP-034 do not define the permitted STS state values or their mapping to controller states, so the correct response cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Define the state values and their mapping after the product owner decides them.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-010 bounds the interval between consecutive refreshes but does not bound the first refresh after control cycles begin. CON-SUP-106 specifies a 100 ms timeout, so the watchdog may reset before the first refresh.
findings.requested_change: Specify a first-refresh deadline consistent with the watchdog timeout and the decided start-up servicing behavior.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-029 and SYS-SUP-030 classify and transmit it at start-up, but no requirement provides service-tool access to the cause.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the service tool reads the classified reset cause, including the applicable interface behavior.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires an out-of-range configuration fault at start-up to latch the safe state. SYS-SUP-009 detects the fault and SYS-SUP-042 refers to such a latch, but no requirement actually requires it to be set.
findings.requested_change: Add the required safe-state latch behavior for the start-up configuration fault.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-035 specifies GET FAULTS only when at least eight reports are retained. CON-SUP-113 requires the service response, but behavior with fewer retained reports is unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Specify the response for fewer than eight retained reports, including an empty history, after the product owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 requires checkpoints of tasks released in a control cycle by its end, while CON-SUP-103 permits T_DIAG to execute for 20 ms in a 10 ms cycle. SYS-SUP-006 applies the cycle-end rule and SYS-SUP-007 excludes T_DIAG from its explicit missing-checkpoint rule.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the T_DIAG checkpoint timing and update the flow requirements consistently.
